regulatory_body: US FDA (OTC Drug Monograph / Final Rule)
finding_summary: FDA classifies benzoyl peroxide as GRASE (generally recognized as safe and effective) for OTC topical acne treatment under the Topical Acne Drug Products monograph (M006). Required label warnings: for external use only; avoid contact with eyes, lips, and mouth; may bleach hair or dyed fabric; skin irritation/dryness common, discontinue if severe irritation occurs; not for use on broken or sensitive skin without doctor consult.
concentration_limit: 2.5% to 10% (approved OTC concentration range per monograph)
source_type: Federal Register final rule (binding US drug regulation)

finding_summary: SCCS final opinion (published Feb 2023, opinion number SCCS/1642/22) concluded alpha-arbutin is safe in cosmetics up to specific concentration caps, contingent on hydroquinone impurity being kept to unavoidable trace levels only. The EU codified this into binding law via Regulation (EU) 2024/996 (adopted 3 April 2024), which added alpha-arbutin and arbutin to Annex III (restricted substances) of the EU Cosmetics Regulation. Compliance deadline for placing product on market: 1 Feb 2025; non-compliant stock withdrawal deadline: 1 Nov 2025.
concentration_limit: Alpha-arbutin: max 2% in face creams; max 0.5% in body lotions (beta-arbutin/arbutin separately capped at 7% in face creams)

finding_summary: No FDA or EMA regulatory body has issued a monograph, opinion, or cosmetic-use safety position on topical tranexamic acid — it is regulated only as an oral/IV drug (antifibrinolytic) in both jurisdictions. Best available evidence is a 2026 literature review in Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology (AlJabr et al.) covering efficacy/safety in melasma and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation: topical/intradermal TXA shows a well-tolerated, long-standing safety profile with fewer irritant reactions than hydroquinone, no reported systemic adverse events (no thromboembolic events) in topical-use studies reviewed. NOTE: this is literature-based, not a regulatory finding — flag to chatbot users accordingly.
concentration_limit: not specified in source found (typical studied topical concentrations are 2-5% but no regulatory cap exists)
